**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Publish freeze.json atomically**

If `writeFile` fails after partially creating `freeze.json`, `withExperimentLock` releases the lock but leaves the incomplete destination behind; subsequent freezes refuse to overwrite it, while diagnostic runners treat its mere existence as closing the experiment. Recovery therefore requires deleting a file presented as immutable historical evidence. Write the complete receipt to a sibling temporary file and rename it into place only after the write succeeds.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the published v5 manifest byte-for-byte**

The newly added v5 `--check` parses `manifest.json` before comparison, so re-indenting, reordering, or adding whitespace still returns `PASS` while changing the SHA-256 explicitly published in `README.md` and the round-6 review. This silently invalidates the immutable v5 identifier; compare the raw manifest bytes to the fixed published hash or archive and verify the exact bytes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject the reserved budget-lock attempt name**

For a pre-freeze rules or Qwen diagnostic, `--out .../results/.deepseek-budget.lock` passes this name check and is created as an ordinary immutable attempt directory. Every later DeepSeek run then fails to acquire its reservation lock, and `createFreeze()` explicitly rejects the same entry, so the experiment cannot proceed without renaming or deleting recorded attempt evidence. Reject this reserved basename before creating the attempt.
